question_text: A 38-year-old man comes to the physician because of upper abdominal discomfort for 2 weeks. He has had 3–4 episodes of vomiting during this period. Over the last year, he has had frequent episodes of abdominal pain at night that were relieved by eating. He underwent a right shoulder surgery 6 weeks ago. He has no history of serious illness. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 14 years. He drinks one to two beers daily. He has a history of illicit drug use, but has not used for the past 15 years. He is sexually active with three female partners and uses condoms inconsistently. His only medication is daily naproxen. He returned from a 2-week vacation to Mexico one month ago. He appears uncomfortable. His temperature is 39.5°C (103.1°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft abdomen with mild tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Bowel sounds are normal. Rectal examination is unremarkable. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. His hemoglobin concentration is 13.1 g/dL, leukocyte count is 23,100/mm3, and platelet count is 230,000/mm3. Abdominal ultrasound shows a 2-cm hypoechoic lesion with some internal echoes in an otherwise normal looking liver. Which of the following is the most likely cause for the sonographic findings?

                    ### Question
                    A 38-year-old man comes to the physician because of upper abdominal discomfort for 2 weeks. He has had 3–4 episodes of vomiting during this period. Over the last year, he has had frequent episodes of abdominal pain at night that were relieved by eating. He underwent a right shoulder surgery 6 weeks ago. He has no history of serious illness. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 14 years. He drinks one to two beers daily. He has a history of illicit drug use, but has not used for the past 15 years. He is sexually active with three female partners and uses condoms inconsistently. His only medication is daily naproxen. He returned from a 2-week vacation to Mexico one month ago. He appears uncomfortable. His temperature is 39.5°C (103.1°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft abdomen with mild tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant. Bowel sounds are normal. Rectal examination is unremarkable. Test of the stool for occult blood is positive. His hemoglobin concentration is 13.1 g/dL, leukocyte count is 23,100/mm3, and platelet count is 230,000/mm3. Abdominal ultrasound shows a 2-cm hypoechoic lesion with some internal echoes in an otherwise normal looking liver. Which of the following is the most likely cause for the sonographic findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Penetrating duodenal ulcer
opb. Acute pancreatitis
opc. Echinococcus granulosus
opd. Liver cancer
ope. Entamoeba histolytica

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with upper abdominal discomfort, fever, leukocytosis, and a hypoechoic lesion in the liver following recent travel to Mexico. The history of abdominal pain relieved by eating suggests possible peptic ulcer disease, but the acute symptoms and positive stool occult blood test indicate a more urgent issue. Given the travel history and the presence of a hypoechoic lesion, Echinococcus granulosus infection is highly plausible, as it is endemic in certain regions and can cause cystic lesions in the liver. The leukocytosis and fever further support an infectious process. While liver cancer is a consideration due to risk factors like smoking and alcohol use, the acute presentation and travel history lean more towards an infectious etiology, specifically echinococcal cysts. Therefore, the most likely cause for the sonographic findings is Echinococcus granulosus.
